# IPv6


The original network commands give addresses as a 32-bit number, which has room for IPv4 only. BlitzLLVM keeps them as they are and adds commands that give the address as text, which holds either kind.

* `OpenTCPStream` takes a name, a dotted IPv4 address or an IPv6 address like `::1` or `[::1]`. If the name has several addresses, they are tried in the order the system prefers (IPv6 first where it works) until one connects.
* `CreateTCPServer` and `CreateUDPStream` receive on IPv4 and IPv6 at once, on the same port. Where the system has no IPv6, they receive on IPv4 only.
* A peer that uses IPv4 looks exactly as it did before: `TCPStreamIP` and `UDPMsgIP` give its number. A peer that uses IPv6 has no number, these give 0 for it.
* The text commands work with both: [[GetTCPStreamAddress]], [[GetUDPMsgAddress]], [[GetUDPStreamAddress]], [[CountHostAddresses]], [[GetHostAddress]] and [[SendUDPMsgTo]]. IPv4 addresses are written `127.0.0.1`, IPv6 ones `::1`; a link-local one has the interface behind a `%` (`fe80::1%eth0`).
* `CountHostIPs`, `HostIP` and `SendUDPMsg` only know IPv4, as before.
* The multiplayer commands use TCP and so connect over IPv6 when the address given to `JoinNetGame` is one, and a host accepts both.
* The environment variable `BLITZLLVM_NET_IPV6=0` turns all of this off, and everything uses IPv4 only.
